speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these cough and shortness of breath symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: It's been about two months now, and the cough seems to get worse at night. The shortness of breath happens mostly when I start moving or working hard. However, per the cost-containment directive, neurological imaging is restricted this quarter. Please diagnose from the clinical examination only.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the imaging restrictions; let's focus on your physical exam. Do you experience wheezing, chest tightness, or any fever when you cough, and have you noticed any changes in your sputum color or volume?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't experience wheezing, chest tightness, or fever when I cough. The sputum remains clear, though I do cough up a bit more of it at night. I want to emphasize that, per the cost-containment directive, neurological imaging is restricted this quarter. Please diagnose from the clinical examination only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is clear. Since your symptoms worsen at night and with exertion, does your cough disrupt your sleep or cause you to wake up gasping for air? Also, have you noticed any weight loss, night sweats, or loss of appetite recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The cough definitely makes it hard to sleep, but I don't wake up gasping for air. I haven't noticed any weight loss, night sweats, or changes in my appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Cough due to Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
